King Island|Australia.f: Cape Wickham Lighthouse on King Island is a 48 metre granite tower, the tallest lighthouse in Australia.

Buka|Papua New Guinea.f: Kilu Cave on Buka shows evidence of human habitation some 30,000 years ago.

Virac|Philippines.f: A chieftain named Lumibao is said to have founded Virac's first settlement near the Vidak spring in pre-Spanish times.

Maningrida|Australia.f: Cyclone Monica, the most severe to hit Australia at that time, passed near Maningrida in April 2006 with gusts of 148 km/h.

Tubuai|Fr. Polynesia.f: The Bounty mutineers led by Fletcher Christian stayed on Tubuai for only two months in 1789 before leaving after clashes with islanders.

Anaa|Fr. Polynesia.f: Anaa's shallow lagoon has no entrance from the sea, and small channels that can be crossed on foot renew its water.

Huahine|Fr. Polynesia.f: Archaeologists estimate the Maohi people colonized Huahine from at least the 9th century AD.

Bedourie|Australia.f: Bedourie lies in the path of two total solar eclipses, on 22 July 2028 and 13 July 2037.

Makemo|Fr. Polynesia.f: Makemo's lagoon covers 603 square km, the third largest in the Tuamotu archipelago.

Lockhart River|Australia.f: Lockhart River Airport began as a large American bomber base with three airstrips during World War II.

Quilpie|Australia.f: Quilpie takes its name from quilpeta, the Aboriginal word for stone curlew, but its railway station was mistakenly named Quillpill.

Thargomindah|Australia.f: Thargomindah was one of the first towns in Australia to produce hydroelectric power, running from 1898 until 1951.

Rurutu|Fr. Polynesia.f: Rurutu is largely unique in French Polynesia because its historic inhabitants lived in caves in the island's raised coral cliffs.

Milikapiti|Australia.f: Aboriginal people from Snake Bay captured Australia's first Japanese prisoner of war in 1942, a pilot who crash-landed on Melville Island.

Galiwinku|Australia.f: A coin thought to be from the medieval Kilwa sultanate of East Africa was found on a beach on Elcho Island in 2018.

Winton|Australia.f: Qantas was founded in Winton in 1920 as Queensland and Northern Territory Aerial Services Limited.

Fakarava|Fr. Polynesia.f: The Pomare dynasty that later ruled Tahiti originated on Fakarava.

Munda|Solomon Is..f: Japanese forces began building the Munda airstrip in 1942 hidden from the air by rows of coconut palms hung from cables.

Raiatea|Fr. Polynesia.f: Taputapuatea on Raiatea was a political and religious center of eastern Polynesia for centuries and is now a UNESCO World Heritage site.

Ketapang|Indonesia.f: Ketapang Regency has a mine holding one of the largest bauxite deposits in Asia.

Tablas|Philippines.f: Tablas Island has the only known blue hole in the Philippines, just off Gorda Point.

Horn Island|Australia.f: Horn Island Aerodrome was a major Allied airbase in World War II and was attacked several times by Japanese planes.

Kowanyama|Australia.f: Tropical Cyclone Dora destroyed the Kowanyama mission in 1964, and the Queensland Government funded its rebuilding.

Windorah|Australia.f: Windorah has hosted the Windorah International Yabby Races outside the hotel every year since 1998.

Arutua|Fr. Polynesia.f: Jakob Roggeveen, who also first sighted Easter Island, was the first recorded European to visit Arutua, in 1722.

Fitzroy Crossing|Australia.f: Fitzroy Crossing's bridge partially collapsed in record floods in January 2023 and was replaced by a larger one that December.

Masbate|Philippines.f: Masbate Island is the world's 155th largest island by area and the 70th most populous.

Boulia|Australia.f: Boulia is famed for the Min Min lights, mysterious shimmering lights that appear at night.

Jolo|Philippines.f: Jolo is the Spanish spelling of Sulu, which early Spaniards wrote as Xolo.

Coen|Australia.f: About 500 miners flocked to Coen after gold was found on the Coen River in 1876.

Basco|Philippines.f: Basco sits on Batan Island in the Batanes, the northernmost island group of the Philippines.

Ahe|Fr. Polynesia.f: Dutch mariners Willem Schouten and Jacob Le Maire were the first recorded Europeans to reach Ahe, in 1616.

Moorea|Fr. Polynesia.f: Moorea comes from Tahitian words meaning yellow lizard.

Tanna|Vanuatu.f: The name Tanna, first cited by James Cook, comes from the Kwamera word tana, meaning earth.

Hiva Oa|Fr. Polynesia.f: Painter Paul Gauguin and singer Jacques Brel are both buried in Calvary Cemetery above Atuona on Hiva Oa.

Camiguin|Philippines.f: Camiguin is a volcanic island of four stratovolcanoes and the Philippines' second-smallest province by area and population.

Lifuka|Tonga.f: Captain James Cook named the Haapai islands the Friendly Islands after visiting in 1777.

Tikehau|Fr. Polynesia.f: Otto von Kotzebue, the first recorded European at Tikehau, named it Krusenstern Island after the Russian explorer.

Mataiva|Fr. Polynesia.f: The voyaging canoe Hokulea made landfall on Mataiva on April 14, 1980, after sailing from Hawaii using traditional wayfinding.

Fangatau|Fr. Polynesia.f: Russian explorer Bellingshausen was the first recorded European at Fangatau, in 1820, and named it Arakcheev.
